D0 LITERATURE CONSULT PAYLOAD — `oeq:simultaneous-union-inversion`

Verdict: the cited literature does not close the continuum, connected, nonrandomized, multiplicative-oracle problem under the frozen assumptions. It does supply (i) a concrete exact construction for every finite legal subexperiment, and (ii) a canonical continuum-honest profile-inversion interval. The strongest honest same-topic target is therefore an exact finite-grid simultaneous-regret primal–dual theorem plus the continuum-honest profile interval, while retaining the continuum constant-factor comparison as open. Claiming that one can merely replace the 64 weights by a measure and “enforce nesting” would assume the crux.

PRIMARY SOURCES CONSULTED

1. Cai and Low (2004), “An adaptation theory for nonparametric confidence intervals.”
   - Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503662
   - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1214/009053604000000049
   - Locators: Definition of ordered/between-class moduli and Theorem 1, pp. 5–7; finite adaptive construction, Theorem 2, pp. 17–22; general finite-union intersection construction, Theorem 3, pp. 27–28; nonconvex finite-union minimax bounds, Theorem 4, pp. 29–30.
   - Exact relevant content: Theorem 1 gives the expected-length lower bound through the ordered between-class modulus. Theorem 2 constructs one interval simultaneously within a constant factor for a finite nested/nearly nested collection of convex Gaussian classes. For a general finite collection of intersecting convex classes, their construction intersects the class-specific intervals with level α/k; Theorem 3 consequently incurs the factor `z_{α/(2k)}`. Theorem 4 states the corresponding finite-union nonconvex minimax bounds and explicitly notes that the resulting `z_{α/(2k)} ≍ √log k` factor cannot generally be removed when k grows.
   - Transfer: Gaussian sequence likelihoods and the principle “first build a union-honest interval optimal on one class, then combine classwise intervals” transfer.
   - Non-transfer: the present exact-rank/exact-strength strata are disjoint and nonconvex; their target is the nonlinear rational completion functional `GA⁺F`, not a linear functional; the collection is uncountable; and no ordered-modulus concavity/nesting condition has been proved. Cai–Low therefore gives neither a k-independent continuum constant nor nested acceptance regions here.

2. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005), “Minimax expected measure confidence sets for restricted location parameters.”
   - Open primary preprint: https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~stark/Preprints/617.pdf
   - DOI: https://doi.org/10.3150/bj/1126126761
   - Locators: framework and test inversion, pp. 5–7, equations (4)–(12); Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, pp. 7–8, equations (13)–(18); nuisance-parameter discussion, pp. 11–12, equations (29)–(35).
   - Formal construction: for a prior π, form the mixture density `f_π`; for each simple null value ζ, choose the level-α most-powerful test against `f_π`, accepting when `f_π(x) < λ_ζ f_ζ(x)`, with boundary randomization only if needed; invert all these tests. Weak-star compactness and Bayes–minimax duality identify a least-favorable π.
   - Transfer: dominated Gaussian laws, measurable likelihoods, least-favorable mixture inversion, and weak-star minimax architecture all transfer to a finite or suitably compactified masked Gaussian experiment.
   - Non-transfer: EHS minimizes expected measure of a confidence set for a parameter indexing one density. Here each target value has a composite nuisance fiber of Gaussian means; the required loss is connected target-interval length and normalized worst-stratum risk, not measure in the full parameter space. EHS permits an independent `U` for randomization. Most decisively, in its own nuisance-parameter section EHS says it does not find one rule optimal for every nuisance value; it only obtains a restricted invariant result. Thus EHS does not establish simultaneous optimality over all strengths.

3. Cai and Guo (2017), “Confidence intervals for high-dimensional linear regression: Minimax rates and adaptivity.”
   - Primary arXiv HTML/source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.05539
   - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1214/16-AOS1461
   - Locator: Lemma 1 and proof, Section 7, pp. 20–21, equation (7.3); mixture χ² calculation begins with Lemma 2, pp. 24–25, equation (7.18).
   - Exact transferable lemma: if priors on two legal hypotheses have common target values μ₀ and μ₁, every union-honest interval satisfies
     `E_{π0} len(C) ≥ |μ₁−μ₀| (1−2α−TV(f_{π1},f_{π0}))_+`.
     In this masked Gaussian experiment, `f_π` is an explicit Gaussian mixture and the χ² Gram calculation already used in `lem:orbit-chi-square` controls TV.
   - Transfer: this gives valid lower envelopes for each positive-stratum frontier and for any proposed simultaneous excess, provided both priors are supported on the frozen legal classes and have common target values.
   - Non-transfer: it is a lower-bound/fuzzy-hypothesis device only. It supplies no acceptance-region nesting and no upper construction.

4. Schafer and Stark (2009), “Constructing Confidence Regions of Optimal Expected Size” — the direct computational continuation of EHS.
   - Open primary preprint: https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~stark/Preprints/schaferStark09.pdf
   - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1198/jasa.2009.tm07420
   - Locators: Sections 1–2 and Theorem 1, pp. 1080–1082; convex-game algorithm, Section 4; general loss/minimax regret, Section 5, p. 1086.
   - Construction: restrict the least-favorable prior to a finite polytope Γ, simulate likelihood risks, solve the resulting convex matrix game, invert the likelihood-ratio tests, and refine support points. Section 5 treats additive minimax regret.
   - Transfer: this is the standard numerical construction for a compact finite-grid approximation.
   - Non-transfer: convergence is to the Γ-minimax procedure for a chosen finite prior polytope, not to the all-priors continuum optimum; the paper uses confidence regions and additive regret, not connected scalar intervals and the multiplicative ratios in the OEQ.

CONCRETE FINITE-SUBEXPERIMENT CONSTRUCTION THAT DOES TRANSFER EXACTLY

For any finite legal grid `Θ_N={θ_i=(μ_i,t_i)}` drawn from the frozen union, with each point assigned to one of finitely many evaluation strata, let `𝒜_N` be all nonempty connected intervals whose endpoints are target values in `{t_i}`. Permit temporarily a kernel `p_A(y)` over `A∈𝒜_N`.

1. Impose every finite coverage constraint
   `∫ Σ_A 1{t_i∈A} p_A(y) f_i(y)dy ≥ 1−α`.

2. For each grid stratum k impose normalized risk constraints
   `∫ Σ_A len(A)p_A(y)f_i(y)dy ≤ κ L_{k,N}`
   for every `i` in k, where `L_{k,N}` is the finite-grid union-honest frontier computed by the same finite program.

3. Minimize κ. This is exactly the finite-grid sharp simultaneous multiplicative excess.

4. Its Lagrange dual uses coverage weights `λ_i≥0` and risk weights `w_i≥0`, normalized by
   `Σ_i w_i L_{k(i),N}=1`.
   The dual objective is
   `(1−α)Σ_i λ_i + ∫ min_{A∈𝒜_N} Σ_i f_i(y)[w_i len(A)−λ_i 1{t_i∈A}]dy`.
   The minimizing interval action at y is data-only and enforces connectedness directly; there is no unsupported “nested acceptance” assertion.

5. Because there are finitely many atomless Gaussian measures and finitely many interval actions, `lem:finite-action-purification` removes the temporary randomization while preserving the full finite risk/coverage vector. Thus the finite-grid sharp excess is attained by a measurable nonrandomized interval.

This strictly generalizes `thm:orbit-exact-dual`: the orbit theorem is the special case with two target values and three interval actions. It is not yet the continuum result.

CANONICAL CONTINUUM-HONEST INTERVAL

Let
`K̄ = closure{(P_ΩM,τ(M)): M∈𝒰} ⊂ ℝ¹²×[−Bmax,Bmax]`,
let `ρ_α=(σ/√n)√q_{12,1−α}`, and define
`T(y)={t: ∃(μ,t)∈K̄, ||y−μ||₂≤ρ_α}`.
Set
`C_prof(y)=[inf T(y),sup T(y)]` when `T(y)` is nonempty, and use any fixed singleton otherwise.

Then `C_prof` is data-only, connected, and union-honest: under every legal M, the true pair belongs to the ball with probability `1−α`. Using the closure is important because the exact condition `rank(A)=rank(M)` is not closed under limits; closed intervals plus Gaussian total-variation continuity make closure coverage legitimate. This construction gives a real continuum inversion, but no cited result bounds its positive-stratum expected length by a universal multiple of `L_{r,s}^𝒰(n)`.

WHY THE ORIGINAL OBLIGATION CANNOT HONESTLY BE CLOSED NOW

The missing theorem is not existence of some honest continuum interval; `C_prof` supplies that. The missing theorem is a uniform oracle inequality comparing its risk, or another single rule’s risk, with every positive-stratum frontier. Such a theorem requires at least one of:

- an ordered/local-modulus regularity inequality uniform as `s↓0`;
- a proof that the composite target-fiber acceptance regions can be chosen nested;
- or a compact minimax theorem for connected interval actions with multiplicatively normalized continuum stratum risks, plus deterministic purification.

None is in the frozen core or the cited sources. Cai–Low’s hypotheses fail; EHS does not solve nuisance-wise simultaneous optimality; Cai–Guo supplies only lower bounds; Schafer–Stark only gives Γ-grid approximation. Therefore neither a universal constant nor the sharp multiplicative excess may be asserted.
